A familiar adventure, a lighter touch

The adventurer’s handbook

WASD / arrowsWalk in eight directions. Walk against a block to push.
J / X / left clickSword slash. Hold until the spark, then release for a spin.
E / SpaceTalk, open, lift, throw. Walk into an open door to travel.
K / Z / right clickUse the selected item. Mouse points attacks; otherwise you face your movement.
Q / 1–8Cycle items / select a specific item. Bow is found inside.
Shift / CBrace the shield and lock facing. Blocks frontal rocks, not melee.
I / M / EscSatchel / map / pause. F fullscreen. U mute.

Touch: drag the left side of the scene or use the directional pad. Sword holds charge a spin. Action lifts and throws; Item uses the selected tool.

Gamepad: left stick / D-pad move · A sword · B action · X item · Y map · LB/RB cycle · LT brace · Start pause. Right stick aims. In menus, D-pad selects and A confirms.

Build record · 27 September 2026

Field notes & completion report

A complete, compact Eastern Palace adaptation, built with the supplied CO55 engine. Original title, procedural artwork, adaptation code and synthesized soundtrack by GPT-6 Astra Pro. Generated 27 September 2026.

Launch & play

Open this HTML file directly in a modern browser. No installation, server or network is required. Choose Begin the Adventure; audio begins after a click or key press. Landscape orientation offers more room on phones. Open the handbook for keyboard, touch and gamepad controls.

Local saves record discoveries, equipment, keys, defeated enemies and your location. Failure returns you to the current chamber entrance with restored hearts and a 10-rupee penalty; boss attempts reset all six knights. A bottled fairy instead revives you immediately. New Adventure asks before replacing an existing saved adventure, or an active adventure with collected treasure.

Browsers can restrict storage for file URLs or private sessions. When storage is unavailable, a visible warning identifies session-only saving: Continue works within this tab, but closing it loses that fallback. Moving or renaming this HTML may change its storage origin. There is no account, telemetry or external service.

Selected level & source checklist

The selected level is Eastern Palace, not the full game. Its source progression is represented below. Geometry, room grouping and traversal distances are compact adaptations, not a tile-for-tile reconstruction.

Source contentPlayable location / implementation
Sage and palace approachEastern Forecourt: guidance, Octoroks and an awakening Armos statue.
Pots, hidden switches, PopoQuiet Threshold and Great Hall; lift pots, step on switches and unlock routes.
Rolling balls, alcoves, raised treasureRolling Stone hall: five small balls followed by a giant; an upper bridge leads to 100 rupees.
Map, Compass, telepathyCartographers and Compass Library; usable map, treasure/boss markers and advice.
Blue Stalfos combatBone Gallery and western chambers; dodging skeletons reward pottery and boomerang use.
Darkness, Anti-Fairies, small keysUnlit Passage, Key Alcove and Lantern Hall; Lamp, powder, eye-guard key and two consumable locks.
Big Key, guarded pot, block shortcutGreat Key chamber: clear the guards, lift the protected pot, activate its switch, open the chest and push the block.
Bow, Gray Stalfos, fairy vaseGreat Hall: Big Key chest, falling skull-throwers and a usable passage to the Fairy Well.
Treasury, upper switches and sentriesBlue Treasury’s 90 rupees; Upper Trials’ green eyes and ball hazard; Scarlet Ward’s arrow-only red eyes.
Six Armos KnightsSanctum: circle, line charge, final red knight’s targeted leaps; sword and arrow damage.
Heart Container, Pendant of CourageBoss rewards, results screen, completed local save and courtyard epilogue.

Source references: Zelda Dungeon — Eastern Palace walkthrough and illustrated room guidance; Zelda Universe — Eastern Palace walkthrough; complete game guide. These links are documentation only; gameplay never requests them.

Adaptation choices & additions

The compact route contains 17 areas and nine chests. Several consecutive source rooms are grouped into a single playable chamber. The original’s item-driven exploration, spatial puzzles, readable combat and parallel-world idea informed the design. Qualitative player praise for exploration and concerns about backtracking, resource shortages and punishing restarts informed quick selection, readable objectives, persistent discoveries and room retries. These are design judgments, not a quantified player survey. Feedback references: player discussion and retrospective review.

Added, not original Eastern Palace content: the optional Echo Garden’s two-world bridge puzzle; four bonus heart fragments; a courtyard merchant and spring; emergency arrow urns; a magic spring; expanded starting equipment loan; an explicit brace control; local checkpoints and menus. Blue and red Eyegores retain their eye-based vulnerabilities, but attack speeds and encounter spacing are tuned for this adaptation. The blue shield blocks frontal small projectiles, not melee attacks.

Sword slashes, held-charge spins, bow, returning boomerang, Lamp, bombs and thrown live bombs, magic powder, net, bottle, potions, fairy capture/revival, rupees, pots, pushing, locks, map and compass are usable. The Mirror returns to the courtyard; in the added garden it swaps two physical barrier layouts. This is a self-contained demonstration of parallel-world navigation, not the source’s full Dark World campaign.

Engine foundation & changes

CO55 v0.1.0 is embedded below with its license. The supplied engine remains the foundation: Game update loop, Input, View, TileMap collisions, procedural Humanoid skeletons, Renderer queues, depth sorting, shadows, hit flash, particles, lighting, font and integer-scale presentation. One three-quarter camera is calibrated to short SNES-like proportions. No alternative framework, external dependency, sprite sheet or bitmap animation frame list is used.

Game-specific extensions: actor compositing buffers reduced from 160 to 112 pixels for the authored rigs, up to six cached static floors drawn at native pixel size, unchanged letterbox pixels retained between resizes, water-surface rendering separated from its collision layer; procedural cyclops, skeletal and knight rigs; hero cap, ears, equipment and shield; dithered afterimage compositing; disconnected-gamepad state cleanup; combat, inventory, scene transitions, collision layers, saves, UI and audio graph. All positions and velocities are world units. Update-driven movement and action timers use dt. New game-buffer art uses CO55.px; buffer labels use CO55.font. DOM menus use ordinary browser text for legibility.

Quality & diagnostics

High budgets 240 particles, eight lights of radius 78, four afterimages and 24 decorative motes/leaves. Balanced budgets 80 particles, three lights of radius 52, no afterimages and six decorative elements. Decorations have no gameplay collision. Auto starts High, switches down after sustained measured rendering/frame-rate pressure, and switches back after sustained headroom. A small overlay shows CO55 version, 3Q view, active preset and measured render cost. The same rooms, collision, enemies, damage and action timing are used in all presets.

Auto thresholds: measured render EMA above 11 ms or engine FPS below 47 for 2.5 seconds selects Balanced; render EMA below 6 ms and FPS above 57 for nine seconds selects High. The overlay measures rendering CPU time, not end-to-end input latency or GPU presentation time. These are conservative controls, not a guarantee for every device.

Audio manifest & source-asset limitation

The requested source-game audio could not be downloaded in this build environment. The Zophar catalogue was reachable, but media downloads and the requested Sounds Resource access failed. Consequently, no source-game recording is embedded. All audio in this file is newly synthesized replacement music and effects, not ripped Nintendo audio and not a claimed reproduction of its melodies.

The requested catalogues are Zophar — A Link to the Past soundtrack and The Sounds Resource. Catalogue access does not establish a redistribution license. This is a documented deviation from the requested placeholder-asset specification.

Every audio asset is listed below and lives in the single JSON audio-manifest script. Replace an entry’s data URL, loop property and credit to change audio without altering gameplay code. All MP3 bytes are embedded; decoding uses one local Web Audio graph.

Completion tests

Validation completed 27 September 2026. Tests used Chromium with browser automation, keyboard events, touch events and the CO55 input/update path. The complete adventure was traversed using movement and action inputs, without a progress-grant or teleport command. Separate saved-state fixtures were used for focused failure, input and performance checks. This is an automated test record, not a claim of human playtesting on every supported device.

CheckObserved result
Complete level & optional contentPassed: all 17 areas entered; all nine chests opened; both small-key locks, Big Key, Map, Compass and Bow acquired/used. The six-knight battle, Heart Container, Pendant and results screen completed. The optional Echo Garden and all four fragments completed; final maximum health reached seven hearts.
Navigation & puzzlesPassed: pot switches, raised bridge and descent, rolling-ball corridor, western combat doors, dark passage, protected Great Key switch, pushed-block shortcut, Lamp torches, upper correct/false switches, fairy-well passage and two-world bridge route. Source routes and added rooms were checked separately.
Combat & equipmentPassed: sword slash and held-charge spin; frontal projectile blocking; returning boomerang; arrows and eye vulnerabilities; lifting/throwing pots; Lamp; placed and thrown live bombs; Powder conversion; net capture; bottle use; potion purchase and recovery; Mirror travel. Red Eyegore health did not change after a sword hit while its eye was open.
Bomb regressionA thrown live bomb originally expired before its fuse. Its lifetime was corrected. Retest: place, pick up, throw, wait for explosion and open the cracked garden entrance all succeeded.
Failure & boss retryPassed: a bottled fairy revived the player during the real boss run. A separate low-health boss fixture reached the death screen through normal damage. Retry restored health, reset all six knights and retained acquired equipment and unlocked dungeon progression.
Saves & restartSerialized progress was restored in fresh pages using a Storage-compatible test shim; discoveries and inventory remained intact. With native storage unavailable, the actual in-memory fallback preserved the position through Save & Title → Continue and displayed its warning. Restart confirmation cleared flags, chests and the acquired Bow, returning to the five-heart starting state. Native persistent storage under a file URL was not verified.
Desktop & menu inputPassed: keyboard movement and action events, item selection, inventory/map, pause/resume, option selection, volume adjustment, mute and reduced motion. Fullscreen entered successfully and returned to windowed mode in Chromium. A production-mode smoke test, with no test hook enabled, accepted movement and opened pause without JavaScript errors.
Touch & controller pathsPassed in emulation: browser touch events operated the directional pad, floating stick and held/released sword charge. Landscape 844×390 and portrait 390×844 at device-pixel ratio 3 rendered; the corrected portrait header had no horizontal overflow. A mocked standard gamepad moved the player; disconnecting it produced zero continued drift. Physical phones/controllers were not used.
Timing invarianceIdentical movement input across simulated 30, 60, 120 and 144 Hz frame intervals moved the player 36 world units in each case, within floating-point precision. This checks the tested movement path, not every possible encounter at every display refresh rate.
Rendering & presetsHigh, Balanced and Auto were selected and rendered. Visual inspection covered the hero, spin trail, complete boss-room framing, dungeon/overworld rooms and portrait/landscape layouts. The final 112-pixel actor buffers did not visibly clip the reviewed hero, sword trail or knights. Integer scaling and smoothing-disabled presentation were retained.
Offline execution & audioThe exact HTML bytes ran with the browser context offline; zero HTTP(S) runtime requests were observed. All 23 embedded MP3 manifest entries decoded in Web Audio. Direct file:// navigation was blocked by the test environment’s administrator policy, so this test used in-memory HTML loading rather than claiming a verified file-origin launch.

Measured performance sample

Final-build static boss-room render sample: 1280×820 browser viewport, 480×320 internal buffer, headless Chromium, 180 renders per preset with the first 30 discarded. Median / 95th-percentile CPU render times were High 8.9 / 12.7 ms, Balanced 9.1 / 10.5 ms and Auto (Balanced active) 8.9 / 11.5 ms. Run-to-run noise means these figures are not a strict ranking of the presets.

A separate real requestAnimationFrame courtyard run sampled 60 FPS with Auto on Balanced. At four-times CPU throttling it sampled 20 FPS and remained Balanced. This confirms a measured-pressure response and exposes the limits of the test machine; it is not a flagship-phone or sustained worst-case frame-rate guarantee.

Not performed: native direct-file launch (administrative block), persistent file-origin storage across browser restarts, Safari/Firefox testing, physical gamepad testing, actual flagship-phone thermal/performance testing, exhaustive refresh-rate encounter testing, human audio listening review and source-game audio integration. No runtime JavaScript errors were collected during the recorded successful checks. Documentation links require a network only when a reader chooses to open them.

Excluded scope & known limitations

Other dungeons, the opening rescue, the complete overworld, a full Light/Dark World map, story after this pendant, later sword/shield upgrades, boots, swimming, hookshot, medallions and other late-game equipment are intentionally outside this level. The game does not claim to contain every mechanic from the entire source game. The source’s exact room geometry and split room counts are not reproduced.

Original source audio is absent as noted above. Real physical gamepad and flagship-phone performance are not verified. Fullscreen availability and local file saving depend on browser policies. Tiny portrait screens have less visible world area; landscape is recommended. There is no cloud save or cross-browser save transfer.
